name: Opening Drive

card.context: The day-1 entry signal for a stock that already has a named daily setup (a base breakout, Kicker, EP, PEG, news gap or 20-day reclaim): a leader (RS 80 or more) above a rising 200-day, not stretched over the 10-day, not on day 3 to 5 of a parabolic burst. Green market, many stocks in play.
card.pattern: A gap of at least 1% above the prior close, then a straight move up from the bell: the first 5-minute bar closes green on at least 2 times its normal volume, the day's low is the open or inside that first bar, and price never trades back to the open.
card.trigger: OTHER: price trades above the first 5-minute bar's high (the 5-minute ORH), bought at market as it trades through, no more than 4% past it. If missed, the first light-volume pullback that holds VWAP; the 30-minute ORB is the slow version.
card.stop: A few cents under the low of the day at entry, the open or the first 5-minute low. If that is more than about 3% away, size down or skip.
card.failure_mode: The high of the day prints in the first 20 minutes, the stock trades back to its open, loses VWAP and takes the stop, often the same day; a drive that closes in the bottom third of its range has failed. Four in ten strict drives were stopped on the drive day.

criteria.statement: Daily setup first: the stock is on the focus list with a named daily setup, a base breakout, Kicker, EP, Power Earnings Gap, news gap or a 20-day reclaim. The drive is the day-1 entry tactic, not a stand-alone day trade.

measure.what: the named daily setup behind the drive

options.basis: an entry tactic only, inside the ORB lesson as the drive-day case: fits C35; D-002's note
also a day trade with SMB's scalp exits (sources 1 to 23)
both, taught separately

criteria.evidence: Every owner ORB entry the dossier read sits on a named daily setup (Kicker, earnings gap, base breakout); Kullamagi (S39) enters the ORH on a daily setup; the SMB trader Rodney wants his opening-drive plays to 'have a daily chart setup as well' (S16). D-002's note folds the Opening Drive into the ORB lesson as the drive-day case, an entry tactic (C35). The app's detector has no daily gate: 45% of its fires were below the 200-day and only 25% had an RS proxy of 80+.

criteria.statement: Price above the 200-day simple moving average, and the line rising: not lower than 20 sessions ago.

measure.what: prior close against the 200-day SMA

criteria.evidence: Check B (hourly drives, two years): drives below the 200-day (1,437) averaged -0.03R at day 20; drives that passed the house filters +0.39R. ONON 2026-09-22 gapped 10.2% on heavy volume 30% below its 200-day with an RS proxy of 2 and closed at the low; B26 keeps us out. The 'rising' test is the glossary's 20-session window.

criteria.statement: RS rating 80 or more, in a strong group.

measure.what: RS rating

criteria.evidence: Scan: RS 80+ helped at every volume level (1x+ volume: any RS 20.8% to 3R, RS 70+ 22.8%, RS 80+ 25.2%). CROX 2026-09-17 (RS 77) ran 5.8R: a learner should see why the rule is 80. The RS figure is a proxy rank, not the app's rating.

criteria.statement: Not more than 10% above the 10-day average at the buy. A gap on top of a run can be stretched before it opens.

measure.what: fill / 10-day SMA - 1

criteria.evidence: 27% of the app's fires were more than 10% above the 10-day. MXL 2026-10-02 at +9.8% is the closest example to the edge.

criteria.statement: Not on day 3 to 5 of a parabolic burst (Bracco's five boxes). A euphoric drive there is the short setup.

measure.what: day of a parabolic burst on which the drive comes

criteria.evidence: Bracco's U-Turn (S48) is a gap-up drive that 'lures in chasers' and reverses on a climax day; Breitstein's best-known short is an exhaustion gap with 'a euphoric opening drive' (S28). B26's parabolic exception is what allows that short above the 200-day.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day on average.

measure.what: close

criteria.evidence: Drives need stocks in play; every source trades liquid names.

criteria.statement: The position is at most 1% of average daily volume.

measure.what: shares / average daily volume

criteria.statement: The stock opens at least 1% above the prior close.

measure.what: (open - prior close) / prior close

options.basis: the app's floor (S55); the dossier's recommendation; D-134's default
SMB 'ideally' (sources 1 to 23)
the open above the prior day's high: Market Profile (S42, S43); the A+ mark
none

criteria.evidence: The ten examples gapped 1.1% (RPRX) to 5.9% (CRWD); the scan used 1%. Check A: 7,576 gap-ups of 1%+ in 12 weeks; the app fired on 52 of them.

criteria.statement: A+ when it opens above the prior day's high and on fresh news or earnings.

measure.what: open against the prior day's high

criteria.evidence: Market Profile's open 'outside yesterday's trading range' (S42); SMB's fresh-news gaps (S15). Scan: it ran the wrong way in this window. Among 151 longs at 1.5x volume and RS 70+, the 108 that opened above the prior high reached 3R 13.9% of the time, the 43 that opened inside the prior day's range 34.9%; a gap over the prior high is also further from the 10-day. One autumn, small cells, but it argues against grading the gap up without the daily setup behind it. D-134's default keeps it as the A+ mark; the card keeps it with the caveat.

criteria.statement: The drive: the first 5-minute bar closes above its open, and price does not trade back to the open before the entry. The first bar need not close in its top 30%: a drive may dip in the first minute.

measure.what: close of the 9:30 5-minute bar against its open
measure.and: no trade back to the day's open before the entry

criteria.evidence: SMB: 'we do not let the stock trade back down against us' (S15); Market Profile's open-drive (S42). The app's 70% first-bar close rule missed LRCX 2026-09-18 (first bar closed at 63% of its range, then 97% of the day's range), CRWD and OKTA 2026-09-14 (check A). SANM's first bar closed at 42%, a dip then recovery, and ran 4.75R.

criteria.statement: First 5-minute volume at least 2 times its 20-day average for that bar.

measure.what: volume of the 9:30 5-minute bar / 20-day average volume of that bar

options.basis: first 5 minutes 2x average: the dossier's proposal; the app uses 2x over three bars (S55)
first-3-bar 2x: the app
the average daily volume traded in the first 15 to 30 minutes: Kullamagi (S39)
the owner's rule, the average daily volume in the first 5 minutes (GRRR, S49)

criteria.evidence: Zarattini et al. (S40) found the edge only above 1x relative volume and rising with it (0.38R above 30x). Scan: the 2x floor did not raise the hit rate in this window; on RS 80+ names 1x+ drives reached 3R 25.2% and 5R 18.1%, 2x+ 17.1% and 9.8%, 3x+ 27.8% and 16.7% (18 trades). Seven of the ten examples ran 1.5x to 2x (SITM, STX, NET, CROX, MXL, RPRX). The floor should be settled by the owner, not by this data.

criteria.statement: A+ when the stock trades its average daily volume within the first 15 to 30 minutes, or the first 5-minute bar runs 4 times its average or more.

measure.what: volume 9:30 to 10:00 / 50-day average daily volume

criteria.evidence: The owner on GRRR (S49): 'If it trades it's average daily volume (2 million shares) in the first 5 minutes then press the gas'. Kullamagi (S39): the best EPs trade their average daily volume in the first 15 to 30 minutes. CNC 2026-11-04: 5.3x first-bar volume, the heaviest in the set; LRCX 5.7x.

criteria.statement: It is over in minutes: the day's low is the open or inside the first 5-minute bar.

measure.what: bar in which the day's low prints

criteria.evidence: SMB 'right away' (S15); Market Profile (S42); the exact window is the dossier's. All ten examples set the day's low in the first 5-minute bar. The scan's 'low stayed in the first bar' split (41% to 3R against 2%) is circular, since the stop sits just under that bar.

criteria.statement: Price trades above the first 5-minute bar's high, the 5-minute ORH.

measure.what: intraday high after the first bar against the first 5-minute bar's high

options.basis: fastest, most noise
Breitstein's bar (S31)
Zarattini (S40), Bracco, SMB; Kullamagi's ORH (S39); the dossier's recommendation
the owner's Kicker rule; D-031's default for the taught window, with the 5-minute drive as an advanced note

criteria.evidence: The owner: 'break the opening range' (GRRR, S49). Zarattini et al. (S40) measured the 5-minute version as by far the best (41.6% a year on stocks in play against 2.3% for 30 minutes). All ten examples triggered at 9:35, the second 5-minute bar. PAYC 2026-10-01: the 9:35 fill was the high of the day; a drive whose first push fails in minute six is usually not a drive. D-031's default makes the 30-minute bar the taught window and the 5-minute drive an advanced note; the card keeps the dossier's 5-minute recommendation and names the conflict.

criteria.statement: A market order the moment it trades through; no waiting for the bar to close.
criteria.evidence: Breitstein does not wait for closes (S29). The app waits for three closed bars plus a fourth close, found by an hourly job: on 5-minute bars the entry comes at 9:45 or later, on 30-minute bars at 11:00 or later, when SMB says the drive is over (5.5).

criteria.statement: Not more than 4% above the 5-minute ORH. If the first minutes run past that before you act, the buy point has passed; use the second entry.

measure.what: fill / 5-minute ORH - 1

criteria.statement: The second entry, the first pullback: after the drive, the first pullback on lighter volume that holds above VWAP and above the opening-range high or the open; buy the break back over the pullback's high.

measure.what: the pullback's low against VWAP and the 5-minute ORH or the open
measure.value: VWAP, and the ORH or the open
measure.and: pullback volume lighter than the drive's; buy over the pullback's high

criteria.evidence: SMB: 'pull in on light volume, and a hold above VWAP' (S6); the owner on TMDX (S51): 'Look for a retest or an undercut and hold of VWAP mid morning.'

criteria.statement: The slow version: the 30-minute ORB, the owner's Kicker rule.

measure.what: minutes of regular trading that set the range for the slow version

criteria.evidence: TRADE_PLANS.md: the Kicker's 'day-1 30-minute opening-range break' (S54). Check A: the stop under the 30-minute low fit inside 3% only 21% of the time on gap days, against 38% for 5-minute and 72% for the section-8 rule (check C).

criteria.statement: A few cents under the low of the day at the moment of entry, which in a true drive is the low of the first 5-minute bar or the open.

measure.what: stop
measure.value: a few cents under the day's low at entry

criteria.evidence: F62 gives the few cents; Kullamagi (S39): 'The stop is at the lows of the day'. The scan used 5 cents under the day's low at the fill. TSEM 2026-09-17: a 1.0% stop under the first bar's low was hit within the hour before the stock recovered; a tight stop is not a free stop.

criteria.statement: If the stop is more than about 3% below the buy, size down so the risk stays the same; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip.

measure.what: (fill - stop) / fill

options.basis: size down by A5: the dossier's recommendation
skip: A3
use the pullback entry instead, when the first range is wide

criteria.evidence: The stop under the day's low was within 3% in 72% of cases with the 5-minute trigger (check C), 42% with a first-hour trigger (check B), 38% for the app's three-bar version (check A). Bigger gaps mean wider first ranges. CRWD 2026-09-14: a 3.3%-wide first bar made the honest stop 3.2% from the ORH and 6.8% from the first-hour close. D-005's default: up to one ADR, take it, size down and grade one notch lower.

criteria.statement: For the pullback entry: a few cents under the pullback's low.
criteria.evidence: SMB's 'retracement high/low' (S6).

criteria.statement: A real stop order with the broker. After entry the stop only rises.
criteria.evidence: D41 for the broker order.

criteria.statement: A gap through the stop on a later day: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if that is past 2R.

measure.what: loss at the first 30-minute low of the gap-down day

criteria.evidence: SANM 2026-09-11: 3R by 10:35, then a gap down through the stop on 09-14; the third sold at 3R was already banked. SNX's hourly drive of 2026-09-21 opened below its stop on 09-24 (check B).

criteria.statement: Stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.

measure.what: R at which the stop moves to the entry

criteria.statement: Sell a third at 3R.

measure.what: fraction sold at 3R

criteria.evidence: SMB scalps when the tape slows; the house sells a third at 3R and 5R. Check B: 27% of house-filtered drives reached 3R within 20 days; most drives are stopped before the first trim. CNC 2026-11-04 topped at 3R the next morning and round-tripped to the stop two days later: trim a third at 3R or keep nothing.

criteria.statement: Sell a third at 5R.

measure.what: fraction sold at 5R

criteria.statement: If the stock opens above a trim level, trim at the open.
criteria.evidence: LRCX and STX reached 3R at the next session's open.

criteria.statement: Trail the rest under the 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one, sold on a close below.

measure.what: close against the 10-day (fast) or 21-day (steadier) average

criteria.statement: Time stop: under 1R after 10 days, sell.

measure.what: open R after 10 trading days

criteria.statement: A drive day that closes below its open or in the bottom third of its range has failed (EAT, DAVE, ONON). A warning: the stop is the only exit.

measure.what: (close - low) / (high - low) of the drive day

options.basis: sell at the close or next morning before the stop: the dossier's recommendation (Spencer expected his BBBY drive to 'finish close to the high of the day', S1; Bracco's U-Turn, S48)
no, the stop is the only exit: A4; D-136

criteria.evidence: D-136 settles 44:6: the stop is the only exit. The scan says the check costs almost nothing either way: drives whose day-1 close sat in the top third reached 3R 36% of the time against 2% for the bottom third, but the stop sits just under the first bar's low, so a close in the bottom third usually means the stop was already hit (EAT 2026-09-22: the stop came first).

criteria.statement: Before the entry: price trades back below the open or the first 5-minute low. No trade; it is an open-test or a rejection, not a drive.

measure.what: low after the first bar, before the entry

criteria.evidence: SMB (S15) and Market Profile (S42) agree; the scan required no trade under the open before the trigger. TSEM 2026-09-17 drove to 2.1R by 9:50, then fell through its open and the stop within the hour.

criteria.statement: Loses VWAP and holds under it: the drive has failed. Before the entry, no trade; after it, a warning, the stop is the exit.
criteria.evidence: Breitstein's VWAP rule (S28); Bracco's U-Turn trigger is the VWAP break (S48).

criteria.statement: First 5-minute volume under its average: not a drive.

measure.what: volume of the 9:30 5-minute bar / 20-day average volume of that bar

criteria.evidence: Zarattini et al. (S40): below 100% relative volume the ORB averaged -0.02R.

criteria.statement: No new buy in the 3 sessions before a report. A drive on the earnings gap day is after the report, so it is allowed.

measure.what: sessions until the next report

criteria.evidence: None of the ten examples is an earnings reaction day in the tables; the news behind each gap was not checked.

criteria.statement: Green market: full risk. Yellow: smaller and fewer. Orange: A+ only. Red: mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day.

measure.what: the app's market reading on the trigger day

criteria.evidence: The owner's 'WHEN' post (2026-03-08, S50): do not force opening-range trades in a bad market. RVTY 2026-10-06 was one of four strict fires that day (with NVT, ARKG, CIBR), all stopped: the drives were real for five minutes and the market was not.

criteria.statement: A cue: the Nasdaq trending above its rising 10 and 20-day averages, with strong breadth at the open on a broad gap-up.

measure.what: Nasdaq close against its 10-day and 20-day averages

criteria.evidence: The owner, 2026-03-08: 'The simple one made notorious by Quallamaggie is a market that the Nasdaq is trending higher above a rising 10 and 20 period moving average.' Bracco, 2026-09-20: 'At the open we saw the highest Nasdaq advance decline print since the gap up (ceasefire day) on April 8th earlier this year.'

criteria.statement: A cue: a strong group gapping together, and earnings season or big news days when many stocks are in play.
criteria.evidence: CRWD, OKTA and FTNT, all software, on 2026-09-14; NET the same day; LRCX and STX on 2026-09-18. SMB: 'during earnings season' (S15).

criteria.statement: The short mirror, the opening drive down: a gap down of 1% or more on bad news, a red first 5-minute bar, no trade back to the open, first 5-minute volume 2 times its average or more, below the 200-day, RS 20 or lower, in the weakest groups, a normal borrow; short the break of the first 5-minute low; stop a few cents above the high of the day.

measure.what: intraday low after the first bar against the first 5-minute bar's low
measure.and: gap down >= 1%; prior close < 200-day SMA; RS rating <= 20

options.basis: teach the drive down below the 200-day: D47; SMB trades it (CTSH, JAZZ, BIDU, S7); the dossier's recommendation
leave shorts to the parabolic short (the U-Turn) only

criteria.evidence: Scan: the strict short mirror fired 57 times, 15.8% reached 3R and 3.5% reached 5R, 91.2% stopped. D48 for the borrow.

criteria.statement: The failed up-drive, the U-Turn, is a different setup: a parabolic climax-day short, allowed above the 200-day only because it is parabolic. It belongs to the Parabolic Short.

measure.what: setup used for a gap-up drive that reverses on a climax day

criteria.evidence: Bracco (S48): the U-Turn 'begins with a gap-up and an opening range breakout, driving an upward trend at the open', then the VWAP break and the day's-low break. B26's parabolic exception.

criteria.statement: The parabolic long exception: a gap up that drives on the day after a burst down can be taken below the 200-day; that is the Parabolic Long's entry, not this card's.

measure.what: setup used for a drive below the 200-day after a burst down

criteria.evidence: B26: no longs below the 200-day unless it is a parabolic long.

a_plus: od.role: a clean daily setup (base breakout, Kicker, EP) in a leader with RS 90 or more in a leading group
od.gap_over_pdh: fresh news or earnings, and the stock opens above the prior day's high (the scan's one window said the opposite; see conflicts)
od.volume_a_plus: first 5-minute volume 4 times its average or more, or the average daily volume traded in the first 15 to 30 minutes
od.low_in_first_bar: the open is the low of the day and is never revisited; a steady slope with candles that shrink, not grow
od.inv_vwap: holds above VWAP all morning
od.stop_width: stop within 3% and not stretched over the 10-day
od.market_reading: Green, a broad gap with strong breadth, the group moving together (od.nasdaq_trend, od.group_move); in Orange only if everything else grades A+ (F65)
b_minus: od.role: no daily setup, no news
od.gap_floor: a gap of 1% to 2% inside the prior day's range on average volume
od.inv_back_to_open: the first minutes chop back to the open
od.not_parabolic: day 3 to 5 of a parabolic burst; growing candles outside the upper Bollinger Band
od.not_stretched: stretched more than 10% over the 10-day
od.stop_width: a stop that must be wider than 5%
no_trade: od.above_200: below the 200-day (unless it is the parabolic long)
od.inv_back_to_open: price traded back below the open before the entry
od.inv_volume_under_average: first 5-minute volume under its average
od.no_chase: more than 4% past the 5-minute ORH
od.liquidity: under $10 or under $20 million a day

lookalikes.tell: Check the clock and the low. A drive sets the day's low in the first 5-minute bar and is bought over that bar's high by about 9:40. An ORB waits for the full 9:30 to 10:00 range and buys the first trade through its high after 10:00. The ORB is the slow version of the same day.

Measure the gap and name the news. An EP needs a gap of 10% or more on a named catalyst in a neglected name. A drive can be a 1% gap in a leader already in a daily setup; on an EP day the drive is often its day-1 entry, but the gap size and the neglect are the EP's tests, not the drive's.

Look at yesterday. A Kicker needs a real red day before the gap and buys over that red day's high or the 30-minute range. A drive has no red-day requirement and buys the 5-minute high; a Kicker that drives from the bell is both, and the Kicker's rules (its 3.5% stop cap) win.

Count the up days. A drive on day 3 to 5 of a burst, with growing candles outside the upper band and a euphoric open, is the U-Turn short setup, not a long: the gap-up drive that lures in chasers and reverses through VWAP.

invalidations: Before the entry: price trades back below the open or the first 5-minute low; no trade (od.inv_back_to_open).
Before the entry: first 5-minute volume under its average; not a drive (od.inv_volume_under_average).
Before the entry: below the 200-day, RS under 80, more than 10% over the 10-day, or earnings within 3 sessions (od.above_200, od.leader, od.not_stretched, od.earnings_window).
Before the entry: a Red market, or Orange unless A+ (od.market_reading).
After the entry: the low of the day breaks; out at the stop (od.stop, od.stop_only_up).

After the entry: loses VWAP and holds under it, or closes below its open or in the bottom third of its range: the drive has failed, a warning; the stop is the only exit (od.inv_vwap, od.day1_close_check).
mistakes: Buying a gap with no daily setup because it looks strong for five minutes.
Waiting for three closed bars, then chasing. The app's own rule shows it.
Chasing more than 4% past the ORH.
Mistaking a drive for a trend and adding size in the first 30 minutes. SMB: stocks do not trend in the first 30 minutes.
Buying a euphoric drive on day 3 to 5 of a parabolic run: that is the short setup.
Fading a steady drive. Breitstein: losses from fighting this trend were entirely avoidable.
Switching plans mid-trade, from a hold to a scalp or back.
Ignoring the day-1 close: a drive that closes at the low has failed.
Treating a stop-out as a re-entry: only a new trigger is (TSEM, PAYC).

short_mirror.note: The opening drive down is in this dossier (8.6): a gap down of 1% or more on bad news, a red first 5-minute bar, no trade back to the open, first-bar volume 2x or more, below the 200-day with RS 20 or lower and a normal borrow; short the break of the first 5-minute low, stop a few cents above the day's high. SMB trades it (CTSH, JAZZ, BIDU). The scan's strict short mirror fired 57 times (15.8% / 3.5%). Two neighbours are not this: the failed up-drive (U-Turn) is the Parabolic Short, and a drive below the 200-day after a burst down is the Parabolic Long. Whether to teach it is D-001 (question 9).

best_conditions: A Green market with the Nasdaq above its rising 10 and 20-day averages and strong breadth at the open on a broad gap-up. Earnings season and big news days, when many stocks are in play, and a strong group gapping together (CRWD, OKTA and FTNT on 2026-09-14).

management.trail: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one (E52)
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default (B19)
management.gap_open: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63); LRCX and STX reached 3R at the next open
management.gap_against: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20); SANM 2026-09-14 is the case
management.overrides: none taught. The dossier proposed a day-1 close check (sell at the close or next morning when the drive day closes below its open or in its bottom third); D-136 settles it as a warning, the stop is the only exit (od.day1_close_check). SMB's scalp exits and the app's 3x first-bar target are not ours.

base_rate.window: 20 sessions forward on 5-minute bars, fixed stop 5 cents under the day's low at the fill, no trims, no breakeven, no day-1 close exit; 2026-08-17 to 2026-11-06 (59 sessions, the 1,000 most-traded names, ETFs included: UCO, ARKG twice, CIBR); the strict rule: gap 1%+, green first 5-minute bar, first-bar volume 2x+ its 10-20 session mean, RS 80+, above the 200-day, trigger a cent over the first bar's high by 10:00 ET with no trade under the open before it, fill within 4% of the ORH and 10% of the 10-day, stop within 3%

opened_above_prior_high_1_5x_rs_70_plus.note: the A+ gap mark ran the wrong way in this window

check_b_hourly_drives_two_years.note: section 4.5, 60-minute bars, late 2024 to 2026-11-06; the first hour as the drive, entry at the 10:30 close

failures.why: gap +3.2% over the prior high on 2.5x volume, RS 84, bought 211.21 at 9:40 with the stop at 204.95 (3.0%). Best 0.37R; stopped the same day; the day closed at 24% of its range. The day-1 close check would not have helped, the stop came first; only the pattern of 'high of the day in the first 20 minutes, then a lower high' would.

gap +3.7% on 5.0x first-bar volume (the second-heaviest in the strict set), RS 90, bought 229.02 at 9:35. The fill was the high of the day: the stock never ticked higher, slid for an hour and hit the stop (224.09) at 10:35, then recovered to close at 78% of its range. B21: a stop-out is not a re-entry without a new trigger; a drive whose first push fails in minute six is usually not a drive.

gap +2.7%, 2.9x volume, RS 91, 48% above its 200-day. Bought 165.00 at 9:35, best 0.21R, stopped the same day, closed at 13% of the range. One of four strict fires that day (with NVT, ARKG, CIBR), all stopped: the drives were real for five minutes and the market was not.

a 6.3% gap on 2.5x volume, bought 216.48, reached 2.1R by 9:50, then fell through its open and the stop (214.23) within the hour before recovering to a best close 10% higher within 10 sessions; the stop under the first bar's low was 1.0% away. A tight stop is not a free stop, and a stop-out is not a re-entry (B21).

rejected as an example: the first bar closed at 94% of its range on 2.8x volume, but the trigger came only at 9:50 and the stock sat flat for four hours; its 42.9R came from a 3:05 pm surge and the next morning's gap, not from the open. A best-R number without the chart is not a textbook example.

examples.limits: One autumn of 5-minute bars, one market regime; 41 strict trades on 21 days, so the cases are not independent. Only 3 of the 10 examples are strict; 7 pass every rule except one 'my proposal' line (volume 1.5x to 2x, RS 77, a stop a shade over 3%). The news behind each gap was not checked and needs the owner's eye. RS is a proxy rank, not the app's rating; no costs; today's liquid names only. The numbers are a floor to argue from, not a statistic.

near_misses.why: opened +0.43% (rule 1% or more) on 3.91x first-bar volume; a plain 5-minute range break with no gap behind it; 0.00R, stopped at 9:40.
traded back under the open 169.59 at 9:35 before the first bar's high was taken at 9:40; an open-test, no trade; 0.2R then stopped at 9:55.

conflicts: The name and the lineage: SMB Capital's Opening Drive Play (Spencer and Bellafiore, 2009 on) and the Market Profile school's Open-Drive are the originators; the app credits Lance Breitstein ('Lance Opening Drive') with a setup, quotes and statistics nothing he or SMB published contains, and calls him an SMB prop trader (his firm was Trillium). D-002's note folds it into the ORB lesson as the drive-day case; the card's unit is 'none' because no SET row carries the name. Removing the unsourced text is D-010 (question 8); a card and a journal tag is D-014 (question 10).

Day trade or entry tactic: SMB's play is a day trade, often a scalp; C35 says we swing trade. The card teaches the drive as the day-1 entry for a daily setup, held under the house trims and trail (D-002).

The trigger bar: 1-minute, 2-minute (Breitstein), 5-minute (Zarattini, Bracco, SMB, the dossier's recommendation) or 30-minute (the owner's Kicker rule). D-031's default makes the first regular 30-minute bar the taught window everywhere and the 5-minute drive an advanced note; the card keeps the dossier's 5-minute recommendation and the 30-minute ORB as the slow version. The owner decides.

The gap over the prior day's high: Market Profile and SMB make it the A+ mark (D-134's default); the scan's one window ran the other way (13.9% to 3R over the prior high against 34.9% inside the prior range), partly because a gap over the prior high is also further from the 10-day. The cue is kept with the caveat.

The volume floor: the dossier proposes 2x first-bar volume; the scan found 1x to 2x drives on RS 80+ names did as well or better (25.2% / 18.1% against 17.1% / 9.8%); the owner's own rule is the average daily volume in the first 5 minutes; Kullamagi's is 15 to 30 minutes. D-006.

The day-1 close check: the dossier proposes selling at the close or next morning when the drive day closes below its open or in its bottom third (Spencer, Bracco's U-Turn); A4 and D-136 keep the stop as the only exit. The scan says it costs almost nothing either way, since a close in the bottom third usually means the stop was already hit.
Stops over 3%: the stop under the day's low fit inside 3% in 72% of 5-minute-trigger cases, 42% with a first-hour trigger, 38% for the app's version. Size down, skip or the pullback entry is D-005.

The app's detector: waits for three closed bars plus a fourth close on an hourly job (entries at 9:45 or 11:00 or later), requires a 70% first-bar close that throws out LRCX, CRWD and OKTA, has no 200-day, RS, liquidity, stretch or earnings gate (45% of fires below the 200-day), prints a 3x first-bar target with a median reward-to-risk of 1.8 that was hit 4% of the time, and puts no buffer under the stop. It fired on 52 of 7,576 gap-ups in 12 weeks.
Breitstein's own writing contradicts the app's prior-day-close filter credited to him: his best-known short fades a euphoric opening drive.

Measured edge: no published test of the drive as a swing entry exists; Zarattini et al. is the proxy (the 5-minute ORB in the first candle's direction on stocks in play, a same-day trade). Check B's drives below the 200-day lost money and the house-filtered drives with a 3% stop did best (+0.58R at day 20), but every group's median is -1R: most trades are stopped and the average depends on a few big winners.

Only 3 of the 10 examples pass the strict rule; the other 7 pass every rule except one 'my proposal' line. The dossier's own 8.9 models (LRCX, SITM, CRWD) were confirmed; ARKG is an ETF and TER rests on hourly bars only.
